newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH POLICE STOP YOUTH CLASH DURING POPE TRIP.
newsitem.headline: POLISH POLICE STOP YOUTH CLASH DURING POPE TRIP.

text.p: Police moved fast to prevent a clash between rival youth groups during the Pope's visit to Wroclaw in southwest Poland on Saturday and briefly detained more than a dozen people, a police spokesman said.

"We acted before trouble could start by dispersing the gathering and taking more than a dozen of the most active demonstrators to the police station," Wroclaw province police spokesman Stanislaw Sztygar told Reuters.
He said the brief incident, which did not take place within sight of Pope John Paul ll, involved about 90 youths including nationalist skinheads and their anarchist foes.

"We moved in about two hours after a number of youths began gathering outside the Opera building, when a nationalist group began chanting 'Long live the Pope' and their opponents looked set to react with hostility," Sztygar said.
The anarchists, a youth subculture, take an anti-Church line and some had said they would stage protests in Wroclaw during the trip, while skinheads came to hold counter-protests.

Earlier this week, Interior Minister Leszek Miller said he would spare no effort to prevent anyone disrupting the Pope's 11-day visit to his homeland, which began on Saturday. Police made clear they would allow no protests anywhere near the Pope.

On Thursday, gay activist Jaroslaw Blandzinski told Gazeta Wyborcza daily he had dropped plans to summon thousands of homosexuals and lesbians from Poland and neighbouring Germany to Wroclaw during a Catholic congress attended by the Pontiff.
